extracted.intended_audience: Presbyters, ministers, and members of Scottish covenanted churches (critique addressed to Associate Seceders)
extracted.subtask_description: An official Presbytery testimony condemning the doctrines, scriptural interpretations, worship practices, and political postures of the Associate Presbytery (Seceders), setting out standards of faithfulness to the covenanted reformation and acceptable conduct toward magistracy, prayer, and covenant obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity to the national covenants and articles
rubrics_metrics.description: An authority or principle is unacceptable if it stands 'upon the footing of the destruction of the covenanted union,' and is 'contradictory' to the national articles (e.g., fourth and fifth) that bind the kingdoms to remain conjoined in the covenanted union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Presbytery must insist on doctrines and practices that preserve and do not undermine the covenanted union and the national articles. Anti-pattern: owning or pleading for a national constitution 'established upon the ruins of a covenanted work of reformation' (as Seceders do) is condemned and said to 'open a wide door to Jacobitism.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to defend those in the League and Covenant; no defection
rubrics_metrics.description: The sixth article obliges 'a defending of all that enter into that League and Covenant, and never to suffer ourselves to be divided, and make defection to the contrary part.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presbyterial testimony and practice must defend covenanting parties and not countenance or assist enemies of the covenant. Anti-pattern: defending or pleading for enemies of the covenant or making defection to the contrary part is 'a manifest contradiction' and condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magistrate legitimacy requires scriptural qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The word of God requires essential qualifications for lawful Christian magistrates; it is erroneous to assert that anyone acknowledged by civil society is thereby a lawful magistrate despite lacking scripture qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of a magistrate's lawfulness must consider scripture qualifications and the covenants and fundamental laws of the kingdoms. Anti-pattern: the Seceders' tenet that 'whosoever are set up, and while they continue to be acknowledged by civil society, are lawful magistrates, though destitute of scripture qualifications' is explicitly rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scripture must not be wrested to justify obedience to unlawful rulers
rubrics_metrics.description: Texts quoted (Prov. xxvi.21; Eccles. x.4; Luke xx.25; Rom. xiii; Titus iii; 1 Pet. ii) do not prove duty to submit for conscience's sake to sinful or unlawful authority; to apply them so is 'a wresting of scripture.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exegesis must respect context and the moral/legal boundaries of the texts. Example abuses given: Seceders' strained interpretations of Prov. xxvi.21, Eccles. x.4, Luke xx.25, Rom. xiii, Titus iii, and 1 Pet. ii are called 'perverting and misapplying the blessed scriptures.' Use of these texts must distinguish between obedience to lawful (moral) powers and mere fact-of-rule acknowledged by civil society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience is due only to moral (lawful) powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The apostle's references (e.g., Rom. xiii) speak of a 'moral' power — a power lawful in matter, person, title and investiture; illegitimacy in any of these makes the power null as moral authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating civil authority, require legitimacy in matter, person, title, and manner of investiture. Anti-pattern: treating providential or de facto rule as a moral warrant for conscience-bound obedience (the Seceders' application is condemned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prayer must be constrained by God's will and covenant fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: While it is a duty 'to pray for all men' (1 Tim. ii), such prayer is 'not to be understood in an unlimited sense, but with submission to the will of God'; it is wrong to pray for the success or preservation of wicked rulers or Erastian constitutions opposed to God's law and the covenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prayers and forms must not solicit God's blessing on constitutional arrangements or rulers that contradict the covenanted reformation. Example: the Associate Synod's pattern prayer asking God to 'abundantly bless our sovereign king George' and preserve the Hanoverian succession is criticized as approving an Erastian constitution and thus being without scriptural warrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worship and public prayers must bear faithful testimony against enemies of Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: Worship practice — particularly the duty and forms of prayer used by ministers and imposed on people — must not express 'superlative loyalty unto the prelatic possessors of power' or homologate anti-christian civil-ecclesiastical constitutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms of prayer and ministerial practice should testify against Erastianism and prelacy rather than promote them. Anti-pattern: forms that implicitly approve the English hierarchy or civil arrangements that support prelacy are called corruptions in worship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid self-contradictory liturgy and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: It is inconsistent to pray for the 'revival of our covenanted reformation' while simultaneously praying for the preservation of a constitution (e.g., Hanoverian succession, parliaments) that 'is a mighty bar' and 'gravestone' in the way of reformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confessions, petitions, and public actions must be coherent: aims declared (revival of reformation) must not be undermined by other elements of worship or political petitions. The Presbytery calls the Seceders' prayers 'flat contradiction.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject teachings that open the way to Jacobitism or submission to papists
rubrics_metrics.description: If every prevailing government must be implicitly acknowledged, then a 'popish' pretender set on the throne would demand obedience; such a doctrine would 'open a wide door to Jacobitism' and is therefore dangerous and unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrines must preserve the constitutional exclusion of papists and prelatists from the throne and resist any principle that would make subjects obliged to submit to anti-Christian usurpers. Anti-pattern: arguments that imply unconditional submission to any prevailing power are condemned as facilitating Jacobitism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfulness in covenant obligations; treachery in covenant is heinous
rubrics_metrics.description: Violating or treacherously departing from the solemn covenants and reformation is a grave sin; the Presbytery testifies against parties they charge with 'treachery in covenant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covenant fidelity is a paramount evaluative standard: conduct and doctrine must uphold national and ecclesiastical covenants. Anti-pattern: pleading for the lawfulness of constitutions or acts that betray covenantal commitments is condemned as treachery.
